words.gloss: are indeed of the nature of

literal: Even if hearing, not hearing nature indeed are, by listening, to be pierced not undergone, ears.
translation: Ears that have not been pierced by listening to wise instructions, even if they can hear, are indeed of the nature of the deaf.
modern: கேள்வி அறிவினால் துளைக்கப்படாத காதுகள், கேட்கும் தன்மை உடையனவாக இருந்தாலும், கேட்காத செவிடான தன்மையையே உடையனவாகும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme value of learning through listening. The poet uses a powerful metaphor, comparing ears that have not been 'pierced' or opened by listening to wise teachings to those of a deaf person. Even if these ears can physically hear sounds, they are functionally useless because they do not absorb meaningful knowledge. True hearing is not just the physical perception of sound, but the active reception of wisdom.
